{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRCof88AAAABZdtL-w", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn7ElzhDE4fs", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn7El", "number": 61, "title": "Implement Ap uPD4990A serial calendar reads driven by guest clocks", "body": "## Problem

The Ap profile has no working RTC read path. [Bus::input](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/96089f2376ff0ddc7a08efaece6da2f9d531f0e9/src/bus.rs#L393) returns constant `38h` at port `33h`, port `20h` writes have no RTC implementation, and [INT 1Ch/AH=00](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/96089f2376ff0ddc7a08efaece6da2f9d531f0e9/src/firmware.rs#L404) always returns 2026-01-01 00:00:00. DOS programs cannot read advancing calendar time through either interface.

Implement one bounded behavior: the Ap clock/calendar read path, including the serial protocol and coherent synthetic BIOS queries.

## Expected outcome

Ap guests can read an advancing, deterministically initialized calendar through documented RTC ports and BIOS INT 1Ch/AH=00. Both interfaces use one clock/calendar state. Serial snapshots remain stable while the underlying calendar advances.

Hardware contract:

- Port `20h` writes carry C0–C2 in bits 0–2, STB in bit 3, CLK in bit 4 and DATA IN in bit 5. DATA OUT appears at port `33h`, bit 0. Preserve that port’s other existing inputs. See the [PC-9800 Technical Data Book HARDWARE, calendar chapter, printed p.127, and system-port chapter, p.137](https://vtda.org/docs/computing/NEC/PC-9800TechnicalDataBookHARDWARE%2BOCR_1993.pdf).
- Implement parallel commands `000` Register Hold, `001` Register Shift and `011` Time Read, plus serial-command entry `111` and corresponding four-bit read/hold/shift commands. Support 40-bit compatibility and 52-bit serial transfers; the latter contains 48 calendar bits and four command bits. Time Read captures the counter; Shift exposes its LSB. Follow the STB/CLK timing diagrams, including trailing-edge CPU sampling. Retain the serial command register’s documented independent shifting behavior.
- Calendar order is seconds, minutes, hours, day, weekday/month, then year in extended transfers. Fields use BCD except hexadecimal month. Honor 24-hour counting, weekday rollover and the documented distinction between compatibility-mode and extended-mode year/leap handling. Hold/Time Read DATA OUT has the specified 1 Hz behavior. See the manufacturer’s [NEC uPD4990A datasheet, printed pp.4–8 and Figures 2–5](https://www.renesas.com/en/document/dst/upd4990a-data-sheet).

Use the existing 8 MHz guest scheduler. Retain fractional elapsed time across tick batches; host wall time and browser animation timing must not determine RTC advancement. Cold construction defaults to the existing 2026-01-01 Thursday epoch, with an explicit deterministic initialization mechanism for original tests. Preserve the running calendar and fractional time across `Machine::reset`; document the serial-interface reset policy.

BIOS AH=00 returns one coherent six-byte snapshot using the existing buffer format: BCD year, hexadecimal month/high nibble plus weekday/low nibble, BCD day, hour, minute and second. Preserve its existing caller-register, flag and destination-address behavior. AH=02 remains the separate interval callback service.

## Context and reproduction

Baseline: `96089f2376ff0ddc7a08efaece6da2f9d531f0e9`. The supplied open-Issue list is empty; this behavior is absent from the supplied completed-improvement history.

Source reproduction for the Coordinator: execute an original Ap guest that strobes Time Read and shifts DATA OUT through `IN 33h`; compare successive BIOS AH=00 queries after advancing guest execution by a second. The baseline provides constant port data and a fixed BIOS date. Existing [tests/timer.rs](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/96089f2376ff0ddc7a08efaece6da2f9d531f0e9/tests/timer.rs) exercises AH=02 rather than RTC reads.

Project progress: merged Issue #59 adds bounded V30 carry-repeat support. The [Coordinator’s PR #60 report](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/pull/60) records 243 native integration and 90 browser passes, plus local review without blockers. These results were not rerun by this evaluator; independent review and remote CI are unestablished in the supplied evidence. Limited probes do not establish full hardware accuracy or commercial compatibility.

All 26 inventory categories and their full required scopes remain retained, with statuses unchanged:

- **Partial:** cpu-v30, cpu386, protected-mode, memory, pic, pit, dma, keyboard, mouse, fdc, gdc, egc, pegc, text-cg, display-timing, opn, opna, pcm86, bios, lio, integration.
- **Implemented, unverified:** ide, grcg.
- **Unimplemented:** paging, fpu, rtc.

Scope is Ap calendar advancement and read transactions. Remaining RTC work includes Time Set/Counter Hold and BIOS setting services, TP selection and interval/IRQ controls, test mode, and the VM profile’s older uPD1990-family behavior. Those requirements remain outstanding. Protected mode, paging and basic x87 also remain required project work.

Non-goals: implementing those remaining RTC commands, general 8255 emulation, host-clock synchronization, settings UI, Windows, firmware acquisition or unrelated refactoring. Successful acceptance makes RTC partial; it does not verify the whole category.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] Add a focused original failing reproduction before production changes; record its baseline failure and subsequent success.
- [ ] Add original Rust tests in `tests/rtc.rs`. Cover exact serial bit streams, command framing, repeated unchanged control writes, partial transfers, capture across rollover, recapture, both transfer widths, unrelated port-bit preservation and the documented mode distinction. Derive expected values independently from the specification.
- [ ] Verify calendar boundaries with deterministic seeds: second/minute/hour/day changes, 30/31-day months, February, weekday changes and year wrap. Compare small ticks with irregular batches and `u32::MAX` advances, including fractional remainders. Verify CPU instances are independent and soft reset preserves elapsed RTC state.
- [ ] Exercise BIOS AH=00 through guest INT/IRET. Check exact six-byte output, destination guards, existing register/flag contracts and agreement with serial reads when no second boundary intervenes. Verify advancement with IF clear and during HLT, and preserve all AH=02 timer acceptance.
- [ ] Add an original MIT `guest/rtc.asm`, offline `tools/prepare_rtc_fixture.py` and checked `fixtures/rtc-manifest.json`. Record source/license, assembler command, source/boot/image hashes, deterministic initialization, expected results/guards and a maximum 2,000,000-slot budget. The guest must perform real serial I/O, observe elapsed guest time, compare BIOS results and emit explicit PASS/FAIL. Hosts must not patch guest results or bypass instructions.
- [ ] Boot the identical probe in native Rust and production release Wasm at `/` and `/pc98-rust/`, before and after machine reset. Require PASS, exact specified result/guard assertions, unchanged disk bytes, no FAIL/core/browser errors and execution within the recorded budget. Include fixture preparation in acceptance CI; keep generated fixtures outside publication assets.
- [ ] The Coordinator runs `python3 tools/prepare_rtc_fixture.py`, `cargo test --locked --test rtc`, `cargo test --locked --test timer`, and the README’s required fixture preparation and complete native/browser checks: `cargo test --locked`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, `git diff --check` and `npm test`. Preserve existing hardware, DOS/application, VM, CPU and six-game regression assertions and budgets. Use only original/licensed source-built guest tests with explicit provenance; acquire no commercial ROMs or guest software.
- [ ] Update hardware/compatibility and validation documentation with supported transactions, initialization/reset policy, exact commands/results and remaining gaps. Attribute execution evidence to the Coordinator or CI. Review the complete diff against this Issue before merge; no required behavior may be replaced by a documentation-only claim.

## Optional validation

None.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
